name: Persis
overview: Persis is a female believer mentioned in the New Testament, recognized for being dearly loved by the Apostle Paul. While her tribal affiliation and additional details are not recorded, her mention highlights her valued status within the early Christian community.
namesAndTitles: The name Persis appears only once in Scripture and does not have a provided meaning in the biblical text. It is a proper name referenced in Romans 16:12 without further etymological explanation.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Persis beyond the description of her as beloved by Paul. No other relational details are provided in the biblical record.
scriptureSignificance: Persis is significant in the biblical narrative as an example of a faithful woman in the early church who earned the affectionate regard of the Apostle Paul. Her mention in Romans 16:12 underscores the personal connections and mutual love among believers that contributed to the spread and strengthening of the gospel.
